name: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
principle: The product skips or incorrectly performs cryptographic signature verification before trusting data. Attackers can modify data, spoof trusted identities, or deliver unauthorized code that is accepted as authentic.
detection_signals: Java new JarFile(file) on downloaded or untrusted JAR instead of new JarFile(file, true)
Java JarFile(file, true) used but JarEntry input streams are never fully read before trusting classes/resources
JWT parsed with decode()/parseClaimsJwt()/getPayload() without verify()/parseClaimsJws()
JWT accepts header alg="none" or selects verification algorithm from token header without an allowlist
Signature.verify(), EVP_DigestVerifyFinal(), RSA_verify(), ECDSA_do_verify(), or libsodium verify return value is ignored
catch block for SignatureException/InvalidKeyException/GeneralSecurityException continues processing signed data
Signed update/plugin/firmware/config loaded by dlopen(), System.load(), ClassLoader, or installer code with no signature verification call
negative_signals: Java new JarFile(file, true) and every JarEntry stream is fully read before use
Signature.verify(...) == true or EVP_DigestVerifyFinal(...) == 1 is required before data is used
verification failure throws/returns error and the signed data is not parsed, loaded, installed, or executed
JWT verification uses a fixed algorithm allowlist such as algorithms=["RS256"] and rejects alg="none"
certificate chain, validity period, revocation status, and expected signer identity are checked after signature verification
false_defense_traps: Checking only that a signature field exists without calling a verify API
Using Java JarFile(file, true) but never reading entries, so verification is not triggered
Verifying the signature bytes but not validating the signer certificate or trust anchor
Trusting the JWT alg header to choose the verification algorithm
Logging verification failure but continuing to process the data
verification_focus: Does every trust boundary that accepts signed data require successful signature and signer validation before the data is used?

consequence_chains.trigger: attacker-controlled signed-code package, plugin, update, or JAR is accepted without valid signature verification
consequence_chains.consequence: unauthorized code is loaded or executed

patch_principle: Verify signatures for all untrusted code, updates, firmware, tokens, messages, and configuration before use.
Fail closed: reject and stop processing when verification returns false or throws.
Use vetted high-level cryptographic verification APIs; do not implement signature parsing or comparison manually.
Pin or allowlist expected algorithms and reject none, weak, or downgraded algorithms.
Validate signer identity, certificate chain, expiration, and revocation in addition to the signature.

minimal_examples.safe: JarFile jf = new JarFile(new File(downloadedFilePath), true);
